title: Sheafification preserves sections on a weakly contractible object
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $U$ be an affine object that is weakly contractible, meaning that every epimorphism of sheaves of sets on this site is surjective on sections over $U$. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets, abelian groups, or commutative rings on profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings. Form the presheaf $P_F$ by left Kan extension along $a_X^{op}$, where $a_X(S)=X[S]$ is the inverse limit of the finite disjoint unions of copies of $X$ indexed by finite continuous quotients of $S$, as in [lem-weil-pbc-point-lan-affine-evaluation]. Then the canonical sheafification map [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] $P_F(U)\to P_F^\#(U)$ is an isomorphism. This is natural in $F$ and in morphisms between weakly contractible affine objects and preserves addition and multiplication when present.

source.place: Section 4.2, Lemma 4.2.13(1), sheafification/inverse-image computation on weakly contractible objects; exact master RefactorInstruction.tex, proof of Lemma point-pullback formula.

proof.text: Put $P=P_F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-point-lan-affine-evaluation], $P(\coprod_iV_i)\cong\prod_iP(V_i)$ for every finite family of affines, also for the empty family. This is a property of this particular Kan presheaf; it does not hold for arbitrary presheaves.

Every covering of the affine $U$ refines to finitely many affine arrows $V_i\to U$, by the covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $V=\coprod_iV_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-coproduct-evaluation] the coproduct of the representable sheaves $h_{V_i}$ is $h_V$. The map $h_V\to h_U$ is an epimorphism: for any sheaf $H$, two maps $h_U\to H$ agreeing after $h_V\to h_U$ correspond, by Yoneda, to sections of $H(U)$ agreeing on all $V_i$, hence are equal by the sheaf uniqueness axiom. Weak contractibility now lifts $\operatorname{id}_U\in h_U(U)$ to a map $\sigma:U\to V$ with $p\sigma=\operatorname{id}_U$. In particular the lift lands in the scheme coproduct, not necessarily in one summand. This argument also applies to the empty cover of the empty scheme.

Let $t\in P^\#(U)$. The local-sections theorem [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives a covering and representatives in $P$; refine it as in step 2. Write these representatives as $s_i\in P(V_i)$, and combine them using step 1 into $s\in P(V)$. Naturality of the unit $\eta$ gives $\eta(s)|_{V_i}=t|_{V_i}$, so sheaf uniqueness and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-coproduct-evaluation] give $\eta(s)=p^*t$. Pulling back along $\sigma$ gives $\eta(\sigma^*s)=\sigma^*p^*t=t$. Thus $\eta_U$ is surjective. If $\eta_U(x)=\eta_U(y)$, the same local-sections theorem gives a cover on which $x=y$. Refine and split as in step 2. Step 1 makes $p^*x=p^*y$ in $P(V)$; applying $\sigma^*$ gives $x=y$. Thus $\eta_U$ is injective.

For algebra-valued $P$, use the set sheafification of its underlying presheaf: define each operation on local representatives by applying the operation in $P$. Local equality of representatives, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], makes the result independent of representatives; sheaf uniqueness glues it. Every algebraic identity holds locally on representatives, hence globally. A map to an algebra sheaf factors uniquely through the set sheafification and respects operations locally, hence globally, so this is the algebra sheafification by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Consequently the bijection in step 3 is an algebra isomorphism. Naturality of the unit gives $\eta_W P(f)=P^\#(f)\eta_U$ for $f:W\to U$ and $\eta_G P(\alpha)=P^\#(\alpha)\eta_F$ for $\alpha:F\to G$; since the relevant components are invertible these equations prove both claimed naturalities.
